document_title: Seasonal Pricing Analysis for Catering Services
purpose: Detailed analysis of seasonal pricing variations, strategies, and opportunities for wedding and corporate catering.

key_findings: Wedding peak season (May-June, Sept-Oct) commands 10-20% premium over off-peak
Corporate Q4 holiday season (Nov-Dec) is highest revenue period for B2B
January-February represents best value for budget-conscious clients
Friday weddings have grown to near-Saturday pricing in many markets
Post-2020: More flexibility on day-of-week for both segments
revenue_optimization_opportunities: Develop compelling off-season packages with added value
Create corporate holiday party early-bird incentives (book by Oct)
Build elopement/intimate wedding products for slow periods
Structure annual contracts to smooth seasonal revenue fluctuations

regional_notes: Outdoor events possible March-May and Oct-Nov
Short outdoor season makes those dates precious
Winter weddings can be magical (snow, cozy indoor)
Spring weather very unpredictable - contingency essential

Weather changes rapidly - always backup plan

notable: Christmas wedding dates popular despite 'off-season' label

january_promotions.name: New Year, New Beginnings Wedding Special
january_promotions.offer: 20% off January-March wedding dates OR complimentary champagne toast upgrade
marketing_channels: Wedding show presence (Jan is big wedding show month)

february_promotions.name: Sweetheart Savings / Love is in the Air
february_promotions.offer: 15% off April-June dates booked in February OR free tasting upgrade
february_promotions.target: Couples 6-9 months out from wedding date

march_promotions.name: March Madness / Spring Forward Special
march_promotions.offer: Complimentary upgrade on Friday or Sunday weddings OR waived minimum for new bookings

july_august_promotions.focus: Fill remaining summer inventory before September rush

september_october_no_promotions.strategy: Full peak pricing - highest demand period
